description: Daily Datastream (and some Bloomberg) data on the 12 dual-listed companies of de Jong, Rosenthal & van Dijk (2009), compiled for academic DLC research; workbooks dated June 2008, plus equalization agreements, prospectuses and press clippings.
license: Thomson Reuters Datastream data: licensed, do not redistribute. Kept in DVC only, never committed to Git.

workbooks: RD Shell data - update and unification.xls
Rio Tinto ADR data Bloomberg - Datastream.xls

calendar: business_daily (Datastream pads exchange holidays with the previous price)
known_issues: Dates exported as dd/mm/yy: days 1-12 stored by Excel as month/day, days 13-31 as text. Repaired in quant_lab.data.datastream.

Smithkline Beecham sheets are Bloomberg exports: m/d/yyyy text dates, total returns as daily log returns, both legs in US$; the workbook's H/E price ratio is 2 x the two price columns (an ADR/unit conversion), reproduced in conf/dlc/smithkline.yaml.
UK prices in pence except Rio Tinto PLC price (divided by 100 by the workbook author); UK quotes in pence.
Dutch legs in EUR (ex-NLG); Rio Tinto Ltd in AUD; FX per GBP included per workbook.
Volume (turnover by volume) in thousands of shares, split-adjusted like prices.
Workbooks extracted at different times use different split adjustments (e.g. Royal Dutch x2): never mix files of one pair.
Unilever NV price stale on most days before ~1993; NV quotes unreliable (median spread 165-420 bps).
Unilever NV 'TURNOVER BY VOLUME' is ~0.0007% of NV shares outstanding per day (other legs 0.2-0.7%): not primary-market volume. conf/data/unilever.yaml sets volume_reliable: false.
Rio Tinto, BHP Billiton and Brambles: Sydney and London closes are ~10 hours apart (non-synchronous).

FX per GBP is Datastream's daily rate; its fixing time relative to the Amsterdam/Sydney close is not documented in the workbooks. GBP-converted foreign legs (close = price / fx) therefore may not be exactly tradable at the reported close. FX conversion is costed by costs.fx_conversion_bps (audit 2026-10-07, A5).

Dexia: one-day spike on 1997-12-19 (log deviation -32.4%, reversing the next day); the archive contains 'Dexia outlier causes 19 December 1997.doc'. The paper's Table II minimum (-17.66%) does not contain it. Kept as delivered (raw is immutable). The authors left its two return observations out of Table III (research/reports/dejong_table3.md); the step-16 arbitrage runs report both the data as delivered and the variant dexia_spike_removed (conf/dejong/default.yaml).
Dexia and Fortis: Table II statistics from these workbooks differ from the paper's beyond rounding (research/reports/dejong_table2.md), most likely a different data version than the paper used.
used_by: conf/dlc/*.yaml (all 12 archives, de Jong et al. replication)

not_used.Unilever.zip: not used by the lab's ingest (dropped 2026-10-07, research/reports/data_decisions.md); used by conf/dlc/unilever.yaml
